title: EPMD: A Framework for LLM-Enhanced Ad Auctions

problem.claim: Integrating LLMs to dynamically enhance ad creatives creates a mechanism design challenge involving platform investment decisions and strategic responses from advertisers and budget-constrained auto-bidding agents.

gap.claim: The resulting tri-level optimization hierarchy is described as intractable and requires reduction to a more manageable optimization problem.

contributions.claim: The strategic hierarchy is theoretically deconstructed, and monotonicity of market outcomes relative to bid pacing multipliers is used to establish endogenous alignment of advertiser incentives.
The EPMD framework uses an Investment Policy Network and an Equilibrium Prediction Network to jointly learn resource allocation and equilibrium mapping.
The tri-level optimization problem is collapsed into a bilevel optimization task.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the dual-network architecture as novel and characterize EPMD as the first tractable solution for this class of generative advertising problems.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Empirical evaluations on real-world datasets with GPT-4o-based enhancement report platform revenue increases of up to 1.11%.
The authors report that EPMD ensures market stability and incentive alignment.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM-enhanced ad creatives offer market value but create a mechanism design challenge.
The platform must solve a tri-level optimization problem while anticipating advertiser and auto-bidding-agent responses.
A monotonicity result is used to align incentives and reduce the tri-level hierarchy to a bilevel task.
EPMD combines investment-policy and equilibrium-prediction networks, with reported evaluations showing revenue gains and market-related benefits.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates investment-policy learning from equilibrium prediction while training them in an end-to-end manner.

interpretation.claim: Separating policy decisions from predictions of strategic market response may make complex mechanism optimization more tractable.

application.claim: This pattern may apply to other systems where a decision-maker must optimize actions under strategic responses from multiple agents.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach transfers beyond generative advertising or under what assumptions the reduction remains valid.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the real-world datasets, baselines, evaluation protocol, or statistical uncertainty for the reported revenue increase.
The assumptions and proof details underlying the monotonicity result and bilevel reduction are not provided.
The definitions and measurement procedures for market stability and incentive alignment are not provided.
